illustrae.name:
IMAGE 01 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. A horizontal lipid-bilayer cell membrane band runs left-to-right across the middle; extracellular space above, cytoplasm below. A single receptor tyrosine kinase crosses the membrane, drawn in three labeled parts: a teal extracellular ligand-binding domain (a cup/pocket shape) above the membrane, labeled "ligand-binding domain"; a grey transmembrane segment crossing the membrane, labeled "transmembrane"; an orange intracellular kinase domain (a lobe) below the membrane, labeled "kinase domain." A small purple growth-factor shape sits docked into the teal extracellular cup, labeled "growth factor." Because the ligand is bound, the orange kinase lobe is firing: yellow burst/spark marks radiate from it and a downward arrow into the cytoplasm is labeled "normal growth signal." Calm, single receptor. No molecular structures. Fill the wide frame with the membrane spanning full width and the receptor centered.
IMAGE 02 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. Same horizontal lipid-bilayer membrane band, extracellular above, cytoplasm below. TWO identical receptor tyrosine kinases sit side by side, each with the same fixed anatomy (teal extracellular ligand-binding cup, grey transmembrane segment, orange intracellular kinase lobe). At the bottom, in the cytoplasm, a distinct red fusion-partner segment joins the two kinase domains together, clamping them into a pair, labeled "fusion protein — forces dimerization." IMPORTANT: there is NO purple growth factor anywhere — the extracellular cups are empty. Despite no ligand, both orange kinase lobes are firing: yellow burst/spark marks radiate from both and a downward arrow into the cytoplasm is labeled "constitutive signal — no growth factor." Small optional label near the fusion: "(e.g. Tel/PDGFR)". No molecular structures. Fill the wide frame.
IMAGE 03 - 
Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. Same horizontal lipid-bilayer membrane band, extracellular above, cytoplasm below. MANY identical receptor tyrosine kinases — six to eight of them — crowded densely along the membrane, all with the same fixed anatomy (teal extracellular cup, grey transmembrane segment, orange kinase lobe). Below the membrane, a small DNA/gene icon with multiple copies and an upward arrow, labeled "gene amplification → overexpression." IMPORTANT: NO purple growth factor anywhere — all extracellular cups empty. Because the receptors are so crowded, their orange kinase lobes are firing: yellow burst/spark marks radiate from the cluster and a downward arrow into the cytoplasm is labeled "constitutive signal — no growth factor." Small optional label: "(e.g. erbB-2)". No molecular structures. Fill the wide frame with a dense row of receptors.
IMAGE 04 - 
Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. Same horizontal lipid-bilayer membrane band, extracellular above, cytoplasm below. A single receptor tyrosine kinase crosses the membrane — BUT its teal extracellular ligand-binding domain is MISSING: the top of the receptor is cut off, shown as a dashed empty outline where the teal cup used to be, labeled "ligand-binding domain deleted." The grey transmembrane segment and the orange intracellular kinase lobe remain. IMPORTANT: NO purple growth factor — and nowhere for one to bind. Despite this, the orange kinase lobe is firing: yellow burst/spark marks radiate from it and a downward arrow into the cytoplasm is labeled "constitutive signal — no growth factor." Small optional label: "(e.g. v-onc)". A short note near the missing domain: "no ligand needed." No molecular structures. Fill the wide frame.
IMAGE 5 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. Three small labeled icons across the top, left to right, each a compact version of the three routes: (1) two receptors clamped by a red fusion segment, labeled "fusion / dimerization"; (2) a dense crowd of receptors, labeled "amplification / overexpression"; (3) a receptor with its top domain missing (dashed outline), labeled "domain deletion." Three arrows lead DOWN and INWARD from the three icons, converging on a single central node labeled "constitutive signaling — no growth factor needed," shown with strong yellow burst/spark marks. From that node, one bold downward arrow leads to a cluster of dividing cells — one cell splitting into many — labeled "uncontrolled cell proliferation." No purple growth factor anywhere. No molecular structures. Fill the wide frame: three sources across the top, convergence in the middle, proliferation outcome at the bottom.
